{{short description|Unsolved problem in number theory}}
[[File:Dr. Casas-Alvero talking about Casas-Alvero Conjecture.jpg|thumb|300px|Casas-Alvero talking about the conjecture in a conference in the [[University of Barcelona]] on March 16, 2016.]]
In [[mathematics]], the '''Casas-Alvero conjecture''' is a problem about [[polynomial]]s which have factors in common with their [[derivative]]s, proposed by [[Eduardo Casas-Alvero]] in 2001. 
==Formal statement==
Let ''f'' be a polynomial of [[degree of a polynomial|degree]] ''d'' defined over a [[field (mathematics)|field]] ''K'' of [[characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]] zero.  If ''f'' has a factor in common with each of its derivatives ''f''<sup> (''i'')</sup>, ''i''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;''d''&nbsp;−&nbsp;1, then the [[conjecture]] predicts that ''f'' must be a power of a [[linear polynomial]].

==Analogue in non-zero characteristic==
The conjecture is false over a field of positive characteristic ''p'': any [[inseparable polynomial]] ''f''(''X''<sup>''p''</sup>) without constant term satisfies the condition since all derivatives are zero.  Another [[counterexample]] (which is separable) is ''X''<sup>''p''+1</sup>&nbsp;−&nbsp;''X''<sup>''p''</sup>.

==Special cases==
The conjecture is known to hold in characteristic zero for degrees of the form ''p''<sup>''k''</sup> or 2''p''<sup>''k''</sup> where ''p'' is [[prime number|prime]] and ''k'' is a positive [[integer]]. Similarly, it is known for degrees of the form 3''p''<sup>''k''</sup> where ''p''&nbsp;≠&nbsp;2, for degrees of the form 4''p''<sup>''k''</sup> where
''p''&nbsp;≠&nbsp;3, 5, 7, and for degrees of the form 5''p''<sup>''k''</sup> where ''p''&nbsp;≠&nbsp;2, 3, 7, 11, 131, 193, 599, 3541, 8009. Similar results are available for degrees of the form 6''p''<sup>''k''</sup> and 7''p''<sup>''k''</sup>.  It is later established for ''d''&nbsp;=&nbsp;12, making ''d''&nbsp;=&nbsp;20 the smallest open degree.
